P1.evidence: The application was referenced, which is the right instinct, but as a single fact-check rather than a read-back that makes the prospect feel seen: 'I saw in the application that you run your own company, correct?' The frame was the rep's usual three-part version — 'I just want to understand. What's going on? What have you tried? And where are you trying to get to?' plus the alignment takeaway — missing 'what's in the way' and 'what you need'. Agreement was asked and given ('Sounds good?' / 'Yeah, of course'). Open question ran verbatim in substance: 'what's the main thing you're looking to fix right now?'

P2.evidence: The most complete baseline in the batch and the one place the rep followed the script properly. Age, height and weight all asked directly and in order ('how old you right now?', 'roughly how tall are you?', 'what's your weight currently?'). Work asked and quantified for desk-bound time — 'percentage-wise, 50% of the day you spent in front of the desk or more?' — producing 70% seated. Chronic conditions asked explicitly ('Any other chronic conditions and anything?'). Injuries asked explicitly with duration established ('Do you have like any injuries or anything that is limiting your movement right now?' → right knee, ten years, untreated). Diet asked plus favourite food. Energy asked ('how do you feel, like, on a day-to-day, like, with energy and everything?'). Training history asked but never quantified into a typical week or actual days trained, so P2e is partial. Sleep came out of a working-hours question rather than a sleep question, so partial. Results from current training never asked. The failure is not in the gathering — it is that the answers changed nothing about how the rep proceeded.

P3.evidence: The one-goal question ran cleanly — 'if you would have one goal that you would like to achieve right now, like, what would it be?' — and produced health first, physique second. Mobility/strength/energy as a goal set was never asked. The can't-do-it question was rep-led rather than open: 'Do you sometimes ran out of breath when she's running around?' The bridge outside the physical and the 'what does that do for you' follow-through were never reached before the recording ends. The impact-on-others layer was again supplied by the rep rather than elicited — he asked 'do you have kids?' then delivered the argument himself: 'guys who have kids... they tend to perform better... For sons, you want to show up as a superhero.' No reflect-back.

P4.evidence: Past attempts were probed but thinly — 'did you, like before that, did you do any workouts? Did you go to the gym?' — and the substantive history, a year of heavy training on steroids that he abandoned, came out because the prospect volunteered it. The root-cause question ran well: 'So, what happened? Like, what Why this excessive weight? What happened?' The prospect named the mechanism himself, business stress and cortisol driving stress eating, and the rep confirmed it back ('is it connected, like the stress levels that you have in your work, and you probably tend to eat more when you're stressed?'). Never asked why it did not stick, and the information-isn't-the-problem move never ran.

P5.evidence: The rep was two sentences into the consequence frame when the recording stops: 'Look, I'm going to be brutally honest with you. You're 39... We're not getting any younger, you're 105 kilos, the lifestyle that you're living right now, the amount of stress that you have, and the...' That is the setup for the two-year question, so P5a scores partial on what is visible; the settle test, the 'why not' and the line in the sand fall outside the recording and are marked N/A rather than missed.

P6.evidence: Outside the recorded portion. The transcript ends at 00:18:24, before any commitment check.

P11.evidence: Outside the recorded portion. No offer, no price and no close appear in this file.

objection_plays.detail: Script gap. Within eighteen minutes the prospect disclosed a diagnosed compressed disc, an untreated knee that subluxes on a wrong movement, a blocked hip, untreated high blood pressure of several years, prior anabolic steroid use, and back pain that started days ago after he began self-teaching kettlebells. There is no scripted move for stopping, seeking clearance, or deciding whether to sell — the playbook's known-gaps list covers a physio ruling movements out but has nothing that fires when the rep's own baseline questions surface contraindications. Nothing ran: the rep's response to the new back pain was 'It's good to start, you know. It's a good point. That's good. That's the first step.'

The prospect pre-empted the accountability pitch with an ownership statement that is half objection: 'the change, it will not come, definitely not come from you. It will come from me. You can say whatever you want if I don't do it.' No scripted play covers it. The rep improvised well — conceded the point rather than fighting it ('Trevor is the best in this space when it comes to kettlebells, but it's going to be you that's going to be doing the work') and then pivoted to the kids-as-driver argument.

notes: Textbook baseline — every fact-gathering question the script asks for was actually asked, which no other call in this batch managed. The problem is what happened next: the rep collected a compressed disc, an unstable knee, untreated hypertension and fresh training-induced back pain, and then moved straight into motivation without a single question about medical clearance. Coaching point: the baseline is only useful if the answers can change the direction of the call. Scoring beyond eighteen minutes is impossible because the recording is truncated.
